# Upstream Core API fixes

This client carries workarounds for bugs/gaps in the control-plane
OpenAPI document and its surface. Each item below should be fixed at the
source (the control-plane service's spec generation / route design);
doing so lets us delete the corresponding workaround here and regenerate
a cleaner client. This file is the running checklist.

When an item is fixed upstream, remove its workaround (cited by file) and
delete the entry.

## 1. Operations enumerate every error status with no shared `default`

**Symptom:** each operation declares its real success code (good — 201
for creates, 200 for reads, 204 for deletes) but then lists every error
status separately (`400`, `401`, `403`, `422`, `500`, …) with no
`default` response. ogen turns that into a per-operation sum-type result,
forcing a type switch at every call site instead of the ergonomic
`(*T, error)`.

**Fix upstream:** emit a single `default` error response (every error
already references the same `ErrorModel`, so a `default` is lossless).
ogen then generates "convenient errors" — `(*T, error)` with non-2xx as a
typed `*ErrorModelStatusCode` — straight from the spec.

**Workaround:** `spec/normalize.go` (`foldErrorResponses`) folds each
operation's explicit 4xx/5xx into one `default`, keeping the real success
code untouched. This is the one transform that is a deliberate
ergonomics choice rather than a pure bug workaround; a shared `default`
upstream retires it.

  - Nullable arrays (`"type": ["array","null"]`) — entiredb now emits

  - by-mirror lookup vs mirrorId delete — entiredb ENT-741 replaced the
    two-call lookup→delete with a single delete-by-coords route
    (`DELETE /mirrors?provider&owner&repo&clusterHost`); `mirror remove`
    now calls it directly and surfaces the new 404/403/503 contract. -->

23	### Command Layout
24	
25	The visible CLI is organized around five noun groups plus a small set of
26	top-level verbs. The groups are the canonical home for each verb; legacy
27	top-level shortcuts remain functional but hidden, and emit a deprecation hint
28	pointing at the canonical group form. Newer experimental command families are
29	discoverable through `entire labs` and may remain hidden from root help while
30	their canonical paths are still runnable.
31	
32	- `session` (alias: `sessions`): `list`, `info`, `tokens`, `stop`, `attach`, `adopt`, `resume`, `current`.
33	  `resume` with a branch arg switches to it and resumes its session; with no arg
34	  it opens an interactive picker of stopped sessions (across all worktrees),
35	  resolving each to its branch and pointing at the owning worktree when the
36	  branch is checked out elsewhere. Resume keeps an existing local session log
37	  as-is by default (`--force` overwrites it from the checkpoint).
38	  `adopt` moves an active session from another repo or worktree into the current
39	  worktree and resets target-local checkpoint bookkeeping so future commits link
40	  to the adopted session from the new location.
41	- `checkpoint` (aliases: `cp`, `checkpoints`): `list`, `explain`, `tokens`, `search`, plus
42	  the deprecated `rewind` (functional, prints a cobra deprecation message, will
43	  be removed in a future release)
44	- `agent`: bare opens the interactive agent selector, plus `list`, `add`, `remove`
45	- `configure`: bare prints help and a hint pointing at `entire agent`; flags
46	  manage non-agent settings (telemetry, git-hook installation mode, strategy
47	  options, summary provider). Agent CRUD lives under `entire agent`.
48	- `auth`: `login`, `logout`, `status`, `contexts`, `use`, plus the hidden
49	  `token` (prints the active control-plane bearer to stdout for scripting/curl;
50	  honors `ENTIRE_TOKEN`, else the refreshed active-context login JWT). `logout`
51	  takes `--everywhere` (revoke every session on the active core, not just the
52	  current one) and `--all-contexts` (log out of every saved login)
53	- `doctor`: bare runs the scan-and-fix flow, plus `trace`, `logs`, `bundle`
54	
55	Experimental command families advertised through `entire labs`:
56	
57	- `tokens`: `profile` (hidden from root help while token diagnostics mature)
58	
59	Top-level lifecycle and standalone commands: `enable`, `disable`, `status`,
60	`login`, `logout`, `clean`, `version`, `dispatch`, `activity`, `help`,
61	`configure`, `agent-help`.
62	
63	`agent-help` renders machine-readable, agent-facing usage live from the Cobra
64	command tree (so it always matches the installed binary): bare prints a
65	"when to use entire / which subcommand" map; `agent-help <command>` drills into
66	one command's current flags; `--json` emits structured output. It is the single
67	source of truth the first-turn context injection and the `--agent-help-skill`
68	skill point agents at, instead of enumerating a surface that goes stale.
69	Hidden commands opt into being advertised here by setting
70	`Annotations[agentHelpAnnotation] = "true"` (e.g. `trail`).
71	No-channel agents (Cursor, Copilot CLI, Factory Droid, MCP hosts — no
72	context-injection channel and no agent-help skill template) reach it without an
73	active push. All of them can discover it passively: it is visible in `entire
74	help`, the `entire status` footer points at it, and `entire status --json`
75	exposes it as the `agent_help` field. On top of that, Factory AI Droid (which is
76	banner-only) gets the pointer appended to its SessionStart hook banner, and
77	MCP-host agents can launch the hidden `entire mcp` stdio server, which exposes
78	`agent_help` and `entire_status` as MCP tools using the same live rendering.
79	Enabling a no-channel agent with `--agent-help-skill` reports the skill
80	unsupported and points the agent at this passive path instead.
81	
82	Hidden top-level shortcuts (functional, emit a one-line deprecation hint):
83	`resume` → `session resume`, `attach` → `session attach`, `explain` →
84	`checkpoint explain`, `trace` → `doctor trace`.
85	Cobra-native aliases (no hint): `sessions` → `session`, `cp`/`checkpoints` →
86	`checkpoint`. The `search` top-level remains hidden without a hint.
87	
88	Deprecated top-level commands (functional, print a cobra deprecation message):
89	`reset` → `clean`, and `rewind` (no replacement, announces removal — same
90	deprecation as `checkpoint rewind`).
91	
92	Hidden infrastructure commands: `hooks`, `trail`,
93	`curl-bash-post-install`, `__send_analytics`, `mcp` (MCP stdio server for
94	MCP-host agents).
95	
96	The `hideAsAlias(cmd, canonical)` helper in `cmd/entire/cli/aliascmd.go`
97	marks a command Hidden and sets cobra's `Deprecated` field so the hint
98	renders to stderr on every invocation while the command stays functional.
99	Diagnostic subcommands live alongside `doctor.go` as `doctor_logs.go` and
100	`doctor_bundle.go`. Group roots and noun-group children live in files
